builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation
summary: It replaces fine-tuning a large multilingual foundation model with a small BART pre-trained from scratch on domain monolingual text, augmented via rule-based transforms, masked substitution, back-translation, and one-shot prompting. The cost is assembling monolingual corpora, building an annotated parallel set (here 1,000 pairs expanded to 4,831), running a from-scratch pre-training phase, and accepting that full fine-tuning—not LoRA—is needed to preserve quality. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on BdSL gloss translation with a small evaluation set, BLEU gains may not transfer to other low-resource tasks or languages, and the augmentation pipeline can introduce label noise.
rationale: For a constrained-infrastructure team facing a narrow low-resource translation task, training a compact seq2seq model on a single 24 GB GPU is feasible and the paper directly quantifies the LoRA-versus-full-fine-tuning trade-off, but the approach must be validated on the reader's own domain and data before adoption.
technique: Compact domain-specific BART with scratch pre-training and data augmentation

claims.statement: It replaces fine-tuning a large multilingual foundation model with a small BART pre-trained from scratch on domain monolingual text, augmented via rule-based transforms, masked substitution, back-translation, and one-shot prompting. The cost is assembling monolingual corpora, building an annotated parallel set (here 1,000 pairs expanded to 4,831), running a from-scratch pre-training phase, and accepting that full fine-tuning—not LoRA—is needed to preserve quality. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on BdSL gloss translation with a small evaluation set, BLEU gains may not transfer to other low-resource tasks or languages, and the augmentation pipeline can introduce label noise.

The compact model reaches BLEU-4 of 51.7 (gloss-to-sentence) and 61.40 (sentence-to-gloss), matching or beating four larger multilingual baselines despite under 10% of their parameters; task-specific pre-training yields 11.5-118% higher BLEU-4 and 62.5-90.4% faster convergence versus training from scratch, while LoRA cuts trainable parameters by 99.3% at a 28.0-52.2% BLEU-4 loss.
